description: PRD section 12, T15 (public read-only Hono API) on the mock bundle only. First extends bundle:pull and the loader (T15-01), then serves what was pulled: health, manifest, gates, targets (empty on the mock), OpenAPI and Scalar docs. Records the bundle lacks return problem+json, never fabricated values. The DEM proxy is excluded until G0 requires it. Assumes all of T0 has passed. Stories run in priority order. The author iteration never sets passes; ralph.sh runs two independent reviews and a deterministic gate first. This file is Ralph's task list, not the product PRD.

userStories.title: Extend bundle:pull and the bundle loader to every small JSON the manifest lists
userStories.description: T15 takes over from T0-05 (finished before T15 starts, so no overlap) the files apps/web/lib/bundle* and apps/web/scripts/*. Extend pnpm --filter @terraluna/web bundle:pull and the loader so the server-side API (PRD 8.5) can serve everything small the manifest lists. Tests first. Keep every T0-05 guarantee and test.
acceptanceCriteria: bundle:pull copies into apps/web/data/ every small JSON file the manifest lists for server-side use: manifest.json, validation.json, sources.json and targets.json when listed, and later comparisons and windows top-N files when the manifest lists them. Large artifacts (tiles, fingerprints, models) are never copied.

For each copied file the script verifies the SHA-256 and byte count against the manifest entry and fails with a message naming the file on any mismatch. A file the manifest lists but the bundle lacks fails the pull; a file the manifest does not list is not copied.

Each file is validated with the matching @terraluna/schema zod schema where one exists (manifest, validation). Files with no schema yet (sources, targets, comparisons, windows top-N) are copied after the checksum check only, and the notes list each as a schema gap for human decision; no hand-written substitute schema is added.

The loader (apps/web/lib/bundle*) exports typed accessors for each pulled file, a typed error for a missing or invalid file, and the production mock guard as an exported function the API will import. Absent optional files (targets.json on the mock) read as 'not present', never as an empty default.

All T0-05 guarantees keep passing unchanged: mock with VERCEL_ENV=production throws in bundle:pull and next build, the mock is the source only when BUNDLE_VERSION is unset or empty, a missing requested BUNDLE_VERSION throws instead of falling back to the mock, and an invalid manifest throws.

Vitest tests are written first and seen failing: checksum mismatch, byte-count mismatch, listed-but-missing file, unlisted file not copied, optional file absent on the mock, schema-invalid file, plus the existing T0-05 cases. Tests use temporary directories and do not depend on release/ existing.

make web-build and make web-smoke still pass with the mock bundle. Put tests under apps/web/lib/ named bundle*.test.ts so the exec vitest run lib/bundle check selects them; if T0-05 placed them elsewhere, keep that location and record the filter in notes.
userStories.notes: Ownership decision by the orchestrator: T15 owns apps/web/lib/bundle* and apps/web/scripts/* after T0-05. T7 and T15 may both edit apps/web/package.json and pnpm-lock.yaml for dependencies; the orchestrator resolves that at merge. T7 owns apps/web/app/* (except app/api) and apps/web/components/*. Author (T15-01): (1) Test filter: the T0-05 bundle tests stay where T0-05 put them, apps/web/tests/bundle.test.ts and tests/bundle-pull-cli.test.ts (select with `vitest run tests/bundle`); the T15-01 tests are apps/web/lib/bundle-files.test.ts (`vitest run lib/bundle`). vitest.config.ts includes tests/ and lib/; `vitest run bundle` selects all three. (2) Schema gaps for a human decision: sources.json (ProductRecords), targets.json (target windows), comparisons/<target_id>.json (ComparisonRecords) and windows/<body>.json (top-N WindowRecords) have no @terraluna/schema schema. bundle:pull copies them after the byte-count and SHA-256 check only; the loader keeps them as bytes (PulledBundle.checksumOnly) and never parses them. (3) Reading: "listed but missing fails the pull" applies to the files bundle:pull copies. Large artifacts the manifest lists are never read, so they may live in object storage only; whole-bundle validation stays with export.py validate. (4) Files an earlier pull wrote that the current manifest does not list stay in apps/web/data/ (nothing is deleted) and are never read.

userStories.title: Hono app skeleton, problem+json errors and route-test harness over the shared loader
userStories.description: Create the Hono app under apps/web/server/api/ with base path /api/v1, wrapping the T15-01 loader, and RFC 9457 error handling. Write the Vitest harness and failing tests first. No endpoint beyond /health yet.
acceptanceCriteria: Dependencies are added to apps/web/package.json only (hono 4, @hono/zod-openapi, zod 4, @scalar/hono-api-reference, and vitest if T0-05 did not add it), resolved from current documentation fetched through Context7 or the official docs, and pinned by pnpm-lock.yaml. T7 may also edit that file for its own dependencies; do not touch its entries.
If apps/web/package.json lacks a test or typecheck script, add only those two entries (vitest run, tsc --noEmit) so the listed checks exist; record this in notes.

Route tests live beside the app in apps/web/server/api/ and call app.request() with no Next import and no network. They are written and seen failing before the implementation. The check 'vitest run server/api' fails if no test there is collected, so the gate cannot pass vacuously.

The API reads the bundle only through the T15-01 loader in apps/web/lib/bundle*, importing it and never copying it, and an injectable reader lets route tests pass fixtures without bundle:pull having run. A missing or invalid file raises a typed error that becomes a 500 problem+json, and no default is ever substituted. If the loader lacks an accessor the API needs, add it in T15-01's files in this story's commit and record it in notes; do not write a second filesystem reader.

A shared error handler returns application/problem+json with type, title, status, detail and instance for: unknown route (404), validation failure of path or query (400 or 422, one choice documented in the code and tested), and unexpected errors (500, no stack trace in the body). Tests cover each.

GET /api/v1/health returns status, bundle_version and schema_version taken from the manifest, with Cache-Control: no-store. Its response schema is built from @terraluna/schema types, not redeclared by hand. A test asserts the values equal fixtures/mock-bundle/manifest.json.
Only GET and HEAD are routed; POST, PUT, PATCH and DELETE on any path return 405 problem+json with an Allow header. A test covers this.
userStories.notes: Review finding applied: wrap the T0-05/T15-01 loader instead of a second reader. Author (T15-02): (1) Scripts: package.json already had test and typecheck. apps/web/tsconfig.json (not in this story's files) leaves out server/, so server/api/tsconfig.json extends it and the typecheck script now also runs `tsc --noEmit -p server/api`; typed linting finds that tsconfig as the closest one (without it eslint fails with "not found by the project service"). If a human adds "server" to apps/web/tsconfig.json include, the nested tsconfig and the extra tsc call can go. (2) Validation status: 400, not 422 (VALIDATION_STATUS in server/api/problem.ts): GET and HEAD carry no content for 422 to describe. (3) No loader accessor was added: the API calls loadBundle() through an injectable BundleReader (createApi({ reader, log }) in server/api/app.ts). (4) A MockBundleError from the loader is a 500 problem for now; T15-07 makes it 503. (5) `vitest run server/api` exits 1 when no test file matches (checked with a filter that matches nothing), so the check cannot pass vacuously. (6) problem+json uses type about:blank with the status phrase as title (RFC 9457 4.2.1) and instance = the percent-encoded request path.

userStories.title: Manifest and gates endpoints with typed schemas and cache headers
userStories.description: Add GET /manifest and GET /gates as zod-openapi routes whose request and response schemas are imported from @terraluna/schema. Tests first.
acceptanceCriteria: GET /api/v1/manifest returns manifest.json unchanged and valid against the BundleManifest schema, including mock=true for the mock bundle. A test asserts deep equality with fixtures/mock-bundle/manifest.json.

GET /api/v1/gates returns validation.json unchanged. A test asserts that every gate status in the response is one of NOT_RUN, PASS, FAIL, PARTIAL, NOT_APPLICABLE and that statuses equal those in fixtures/mock-bundle/validation.json, so an untested gate is never reported as PASS.

Both responses are validated against their response schema in tests, and a deliberately corrupted reader fixture (wrong schema_version type) produces 500 problem+json instead of passing the data through.

Cache-Control is set per the 8.5 table (per deploy for /manifest, per bundle for /gates): public with a documented max-age and immutable semantics tied to bundle_version, plus an ETag derived from bundle_version. Tests assert the headers and a 304 on matching If-None-Match.
The routes define no response fields beyond those in the @terraluna/schema types; the OpenAPI components reference the generated schemas.
userStories.notes: Author (T15-03): (1) Cache policies in server/api/cache.ts: per deploy (/manifest) is `public, max-age=60, immutable`, per bundle (/gates) is `public, max-age=300, immutable`; both carry ETag W/"<bundle_version>" and Hono's etag middleware (hono/etag, route-level) answers a matching If-None-Match or * with 304 after the handler has read and validated the bundle, so a corrupt bundle is a 500, never a 304. The ETag is weak (RFC 9110 8.8.1) because bundle_version identifies the content, not one serialization. The URLs carry no bundle_version, so max-age bounds how long a client keeps a response after a deploy pins a new bundle. CDN directives (s-maxage, CDN-Cache-Control) are not set; they belong with the Vercel mount (T15-07). (2) The mock bundle keeps bundle_version mock-0 while its fixture changes between commits, so a client may revalidate an older mock with 304 across preview deploys; mocks are placeholders and refused on production. (3) Both handlers re-check the reader output with the generated schemas (records.ts parseBundleFile); a mismatch is BundleFileError(path, invalid), which the shared handler turns into a 500 problem naming the bundle file. /gates also parses manifest.json, since its ETag comes from bundle_version. (4) OpenAPI components BundleManifest and Validation are the generated schemas under a name (clone().openapi(name), same zod definition, tested by identity). zod 4 copies prototype methods onto a schema when it is constructed, so a generated schema built before @hono/zod-openapi loads has no .openapi method; clone() avoids that import-order dependency. (5) No loader accessor was added; no app/api file was touched.

userStories.title: Targets list and target detail that return only what the bundle holds
userStories.description: Add GET /targets and GET /targets/{id}, serving what bundle:pull copied (manifest targets). The mock bundle lists no targets, so the list is empty and any id is 404. Tests first.
acceptanceCriteria: GET /api/v1/targets returns 200 with the manifest's bundle_version and shipping_mode, and as items the manifest's target id strings only (typed from BundleManifest.targets); for the mock bundle the list is empty, never a 500. Body and footprint (PRD 8.5) are not served until a TargetRecord schema exists, and the OpenAPI description says so. The route never synthesizes a target field from an id.

targets.json, when pulled by T15-01, is not passed through unvalidated: no route returns its records until a TargetRecord schema exists in @terraluna/schema. Absence of targets.json is not an error when the manifest lists no targets.

GET /api/v1/targets/{id} returns 404 application/problem+json, whose detail names the id and says it is not in bundle <bundle_version>, when the id is not in manifest.targets. When the id is in the manifest it returns 501 problem+json saying target records are not served yet (no TargetRecord schema in @terraluna/schema). The id parameter is validated (a documented pattern and length limit); a malformed id returns 400 or 422 as chosen in T15-02.

Response schemas are built from the @terraluna/schema BundleManifest type plus the problem+json schema; no hand-written target record schema is added. The story notes list the missing TargetRecord schema as a human decision.

A test injects a reader fixture whose manifest lists two clearly named test ids (defined inside the test file, never under fixtures/mock-bundle or the app source). It asserts that the list returns exactly those ids, that a listed id gives 501, and that an unlisted id gives 404. Null values are never turned into zero or an empty string.
Cache-Control is per bundle, as in T15-03.
userStories.notes: Review finding applied with the orchestrator's amendment: targets come from manifest.targets; targets.json is pulled by T15-01 but served only once a TargetRecord schema exists. Human decision needed: TargetRecord schema. Author (T15-04): (1) Human decision: @terraluna/schema has no TargetRecord schema. Until it has one, GET /api/v1/targets serves only what BundleManifestSchema validates: bundle_version, shipping_mode (null kept null) and, as items, the manifest target ids in manifest order (TargetListSchema picks those schemas from BundleManifestSchema). GET /api/v1/targets/{id} is 404 for an id manifest.targets does not list and 501 for one it lists. No route reads targets.json, so its presence or absence changes no response; whether a manifest that lists targets must also list targets.json is a bundle rule for export.py validate, not the API. (2) Target id parameter (server/api/targets.ts): TARGET_ID_PATTERN ^[A-Za-z0-9_-][A-Za-z0-9._-]*$ (one bundle path segment, because the bundle names target files comparisons/<target_id>.json) and TARGET_ID_MAX_LENGTH 128. Any other id is a 400 problem (VALIDATION_STATUS) before the bundle is read. BundleManifest.targets requires only non-empty ids, so a manifest id outside the pattern would be listed but could not be looked up. Whether schema.py should adopt the pattern is a second human decision. (3) Cache: the list is per bundle as in T15-03 (public, max-age=300, immutable; ETag W/"<bundle_version>"; 304 on a matching If-None-Match). The detail has no 200 yet; its 404 and 501 are problems and, like every problem (problem.ts), no-store. (4) A handler ends with an expected problem by throwing ProblemError(status, detail) (problem.ts); onError answers it with problemResponse and does not log it. A raw Response is not a valid zod-openapi handler result when every declared response has content. (5) No loader accessor was added; no app/api file was touched.

userStories.title: Unavailable-data endpoints return explicit problem+json, never fabricated values
userStories.description: Cover matches, windows, compare and model. Each is either routed to a 404 or 501-class problem+json stating that the data is not in this bundle, or omitted; decide per endpoint by what the bundle can hold. Tests first.
acceptanceCriteria: GET /targets/{id}/matches, /windows/{id}, /compare and /model are routed with validated parameters (body, family in terrain|radar|model, limit 1 to 500 with default 50, cursor) and respond with application/problem+json whose detail says the requested record or file is not in bundle <bundle_version>. Status follows one rule, documented in a code comment and tested: 404 for an id that manifest.json rules out (for example a target id not in manifest.targets when no window or comparison file is listed), and 501 problem+json, naming the missing record schema, for an id that only a listed file without an @terraluna/schema schema (windows/<body>.json, comparisons/<target_id>.json) could resolve, because PRD 8.5 and T15-01 forbid parsing those files. t15b-api T15B-02, T15B-03 and T15B-05 replace these 501s with real 404 or 200 responses once t0b-contracts adds WindowRecord and ComparisonRecord (orchestrator decision, CONTRACTS b and i).

family=model returns a problem+json explaining that model-family matches exist only when a model is in the bundle. With the mock bundle (model absent or G5 NOT_RUN) it never returns distances, and any future response path that returns model-family data must carry the Predicted label and be refused while G5 is not PASS; a test pins the refusal.

/compare is not computed in this batch. No @terraluna/core call is made and no Derived-on-request value is produced. The story notes record that on-request computation waits for T10 and real fingerprints.
A test scans the response bodies of these routes against the mock bundle and asserts no numeric distance, rank or fingerprint field appears.
These routes appear in the OpenAPI document with their problem+json responses, so the documented contract matches the behaviour.
userStories.notes:
Comparisons and windows top-N files, once listed in a manifest and pulled by T15-01, may be served only when a schema exists; until then these routes stay problem+json. Author (T15-05): (1) One rule, documented in server/api/unavailable.ts and pinned in unavailable.test.ts: 404 (NOT_IN_BUNDLE_STATUS) when manifest.json does not hold the requested record or file (an unlisted target id, an unlisted comparisons/<id>.json, no window file, no model), with a detail saying what is not in bundle <bundle_version>; 501 (NOT_SERVED_STATUS) when the manifest lists the file the record would come from but @terraluna/schema has no schema for its records, with a detail naming the missing schema. The status follows from manifest.json alone, re-checked with its generated schema first, so a corrupt manifest (or validation.json, for family=model) is a 500. No schema-less file is parsed and nothing is computed in place of a missing record. Both answers are ProblemErrors: not logged, no-store. (2) /windows/{id} and /compare decide by the requested ids, from manifest.json alone (round 1, codex-r1-1). A target id is the id of its target window (PRD 8.4: moon-cr-site01-w000, which also keys comparisons/<target_id>.json), so targets.json can hold only ids that manifest.targets lists. A windows/<body>.json top-N file can hold any window. A precomputed comparison of a and b can only be in comparisons/<a>.json or comparisons/<b>.json, and an on-request one needs files that could hold both windows. An id no listed file could hold gets 404. 501 is given only when a listed file could hold the record. An id outside manifest.targets while a top-N file is listed stays 501, because telling it apart would need parsing a file that has no schema. The mock gives 404 for every id. Whether target ids are always target window ids should be confirmed when TargetRecord and WindowRecord schemas are added. (3) /compare is not computed in this batch: no @terraluna/core import or dependency (tested) and no Derived (on request) value. On-request computation waits for T10 (@terraluna/core) and real fingerprints. (4) Model-family guard (server/api/model.ts modelFamilyAccess): allowed only when manifest.json names a model and G5 is PASS both in manifest.model.g5 and in exactly one validation.json G5 record (none is an untested gate, never a pass; two leave the verdict unclear, and the loader already refuses duplicate gate ids). When allowed it carries the Predicted label, which any future model-family response must take from here; family=model is checked before the target. With the mock (model null) it is a 404 explaining that model-family matches exist only when a model is in the bundle. (5) Matches parameters: body is earth only (a ComparisonRecord pairs a target window with an earth_window_id; PRD 6.4 Earth search universe), family is required (terrain|radar|model, no default, distances stay separate), limit 1 to 500 in plain decimal digits with default 50, cursor optional at most 256 base64url characters; unknown, repeated or malformed parameters are a 400 (VALIDATION_STATUS from T15-02) before the bundle is read. limit and cursor are validated although no page is served yet. Window ids (and compare a, b) use the target id pattern and length limit from T15-04. (6) Human decisions (schema gaps): @terraluna/schema has no ComparisonRecord, WindowRecord or ModelRecord schema, so matches, windows, compare and model serve no record until those exist; model/model_card.json and report/*.json are also never pulled. (7) No loader accessor was added; no app/api file was touched. (8) Escalated in review round 2 (codex-r2-1, claude-r2-1): the AC1 rule of 404 for unknown ids cannot be met for an id that only a listed file without a schema (windows/<body>.json, comparisons/<target_id>.json) could hold, unless that file is parsed, which PRD 8.5 and T15-01 AC3 rule out. A human decides between (a) keeping 501 there (404 only for ids manifest.json rules out), (b) adding WindowRecord and ComparisonRecord schemas first, or (c) 404 for every id outside manifest.targets. The full options are in reviews/T15-05-codex-r2.json.
ralph orchestrator 2026-11-14T21:07:20Z: decision on the escalated codex-r2-1 and claude-r2-1 (unknown versus unresolvable ids). Option (a) applies: 404 only where manifest.json rules the id out, and 501 problem+json naming the missing record schema where only a schema-less listed file could resolve it. AC0 is amended to say so. t15b-api T15B-02, T15B-03 and T15B-05 serve real 404 or 200 responses once t0b adds WindowRecord and ComparisonRecord. Resolve both findings against the amended AC0. Make sure tests pin the 404-versus-501 split with a manifest that lists a windows file and one that does not, and mark them fixed with that commit, or rebutted if the tests already pin it.
Author (T15-05, round 2 resolve): option (a) is kept as decided. 7fea61d pins the 404-versus-501 split in unavailable.test.ts with two manifests that differ only in listing windows/earth.json; d4d80a1 adds the rule and the t15b-api follow-up to the unavailable.ts comment. No handler changed.

userStories.title: OpenAPI 3.1 document and Scalar reference
userStories.description: Expose /openapi.json from the zod-openapi definitions and /docs through @scalar/hono-api-reference. Tests first.
acceptanceCriteria: GET /api/v1/openapi.json returns an OpenAPI 3.1 document (openapi field starts with 3.1) listing every routed path and method from T15-02 to T15-05, with request and response schemas and the problem+json error responses. A test asserts the set of paths equals the routed set and that only get operations exist.

A test validates the document structurally with a current OpenAPI 3.1 validator added as a devDependency in apps/web/package.json, chosen from current documentation, or fails the story if none can be used offline.

GET /api/v1/docs returns HTML from the Scalar integration pointing at the relative openapi.json URL, using the package's current API (check its documentation). It loads no resources from other hosts unless the package requires a CDN script; if so, that host is listed in the story notes as a CSP decision for 8.10 and is not silently allowed.
Document info carries the bundle-independent API version and a statement that the API is read-only and that mock bundles are placeholders. No numbers or targets appear in the text.
Cache-Control is per deploy for both routes.

PRD 8.5 (/api/v1/docs) and 8.6 (/api/docs) disagree. The Scalar reference is served at /api/v1/docs, and /api/docs redirects to it (permanent redirect, Location /api/v1/docs, tested), so both PRD paths work. The redirect is the only route outside the /api/v1 base path.
userStories.notes:
Orchestrator decision: docs at /api/v1/docs, /api/docs redirects to it.
Author (T15-06): (1) CSP decision for PRD 8.10 (human): @scalar/hono-api-reference 0.12.20 renders a page that loads the reference script from a CDN and ships no script that the API could serve itself. So /api/v1/docs loads exactly one script from one other host, cdn.jsdelivr.net, pinned to https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@scalar/api-reference@1.78.1/dist/browser/standalone.js (published with hono-api-reference 0.12.20, same @scalar/types 0.28.1; SCALAR_SCRIPT in server/api/docs.ts). No CSP is set or widened here. A strict CSP for the page would also have to admit the integration's inline init script and inline style (its nonce option covers both, but per the package docs style-src still needs 'unsafe-inline' for inline style attributes), and the integration offers no SRI attribute. Options for a human: allow cdn.jsdelivr.net for /api/v1/docs only, or self-host @scalar/api-reference (about 57 MB unpacked) under 'self'. Scalar's fonts (fonts.scalar.com), telemetry, agent, MCP and developer tools are off and no proxyUrl is set. That the pinned script makes no other request at run time cannot be checked offline; no browser run was made. (2) Document: api.getOpenAPI31Document with openapi 3.1.1 and info title Terraluna API, version API_VERSION 1.0.0 (bundle-independent; its major is the /api/v1 base path) and a read-only, mock-placeholder statement with no digits and no target. It lists all eleven /api/v1 paths, including /openapi.json and /docs themselves, only as get operations; the /api/docs redirect is the only route outside the base path and is not documented. Validator: @seriousme/openapi-schema-validator 2.12.0 (devDependency, official OpenAPI 3.1 JSON Schema bundled, no network). (3) Caching per deploy: Cache-Control public, max-age=60, immutable (the /manifest policy) with a strong ETag, the base64url SHA-256 of the body, because neither route reads the bundle and a deploy fixes the bytes; hono/etag answers a matching If-None-Match with 304. The 308 redirect has the same Cache-Control and no ETag. (4) Scalar's url is the path-relative openapi.json, which resolves to /api/v1/openapi.json from /api/v1/docs. /api/docs redirects rather than serving a copy, because there the relative URL would resolve to /api/openapi.json; /api/v1/docs/ stays a 404. (5) Neither route reads the bundle, so a broken or production-mock bundle does not change them; the 503 for /health and /manifest stays with T15-07. No app/api file was touched.

userStories.title: Next mount with typed fetch wrapper and production guards
userStories.description: Mount the app at apps/web/app/api/[[...route]]/route.ts and prove it builds. Apply the hono issue 4877 typed wrapper. Do not touch other apps/web routes or components.
acceptanceCriteria: apps/web/app/api/[[...route]]/route.ts exports GET and HEAD as typed (req: Request) => app.fetch(req) wrappers, not handle(app) from hono/vercel, with a comment citing hono issue 4877. Non-read method exports are absent or return 405 through the app. The mount also routes /api/docs to the redirect from T15-06. The route sets runtime nodejs explicitly if the loader needs the filesystem.
pnpm --filter @terraluna/web typecheck passes with the mount, and make web-build passes with the mock bundle: the build output lists the /api/[[...route]] route and the existing / page is unchanged.

The loader's path to apps/web/data/ resolves under next build and next start, with outputFileTracingIncludes in next.config set for the API route using current Next 16 documentation so Vercel traces the data files. Evidence: after make web-build, starting the built server and fetching /api/v1/health returns the manifest bundle_version. Record the exact commands that worked in the story notes; do not add a Makefile target (not owned). Tracing on Vercel itself cannot be proven locally; say so in notes.

A route test imports the same app instance used by the mount and asserts that a mock manifest with VERCEL_ENV=production makes /health and /manifest return 503 problem+json rather than serving mock data. It uses the production guard exported by the T15-01 loader by import; the logic is not copied.
Mount path matches PRD 8.5 (/api/v1/*), plus the /api/docs redirect from T15-06.

The DEM proxy /dem/cop30/{tile} is not built. The notes state it waits for a human checkpoint: G0 must set cop30_mode to proxy, which has not been recorded; any proxy must be bounded (range limits, allowed host) and the OpenAPI document does not list it until then.
userStories.notes: DEM proxy is a human checkpoint (G0 cop30_mode). T7 owns the rest of apps/web/app; this story touches only apps/web/app/api. Author (T15-07): (1) Mount: apps/web/app/api/[[...route]]/route.ts exports GET, HEAD, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE and OPTIONS, all one typed `(req: Request) => app.fetch(req)` wrapper over the instance in server/api/index.ts (`export const app = createApi()`: loader over apps/web/data/ under process.cwd(), process.env, console.error), plus runtime = 'nodejs' (node:fs) and dynamic = 'force-dynamic' (Next never prerenders an API response). The non-read methods go through the app, so they are its 405 problem with Allow: GET, HEAD; without an OPTIONS export Next would answer OPTIONS itself. /api/docs reaches the T15-06 308 redirect through the same mount. Route tests (server/api/mount.test.ts) import the route module and the same instance; a spy on app.fetch shows the route hands it the request and nothing else. (2) hono issue 4877: with next 16.4.6 and hono 4.13.18, `export const GET = handle(app)` from hono/vercel does type-check (checked with a temporary edit and pnpm typecheck, exit 0; the issue is closed as not reproducible). The wrapper is kept as PRD 8.5 and AC1 ask, and the comment says so. Next's route validator does check the route: a GET typed (req: number) fails typecheck with TS2344 in .next/types/validator.ts. (3) Production mock guard: createApi takes env (process.env by default, read per request) and runs the loader's assertDeployable, imported from lib/bundle.ts, on every bundle a reader returns, so an injected reader cannot serve a mock on production either. MockBundleError is logged and answered 503 problem+json (MOCK_REFUSED_STATUS, problem.ts) with a detail that names no bundle value; every route that reads the bundle documents the 503, /openapi.json and /docs (no bundle read) do not and keep serving. A table test checks the API answers exactly as assertDeployable decides for mock and release bundles under unset, empty, development, preview, production and an unknown VERCEL_ENV (200/503/500). quietApi in test-support.ts now passes env {} so the shell's VERCEL_ENV cannot change route tests.
